## 📚 Rest of the Document (Contextual Background – for full understanding)

Richard Anthony Drago (June 25, 1945 – November 2, 2023) was an American relief pitcher in Major League Baseball who played for the Kansas City Royals (1969–1973), Boston Red Sox (1974–1975, 1978–1980), California Angels (1976–1977), Baltimore Orioles (1977), and Seattle Mariners (1981). He batted and threw right-handed.

Drago played high school ball for Woodward High School in Toledo, Ohio, graduating in 1963.  
He was originally signed by the Detroit Tigers in the 1964 amateur draft, but was selected by the Kansas City Royals during the 1968 expansion draft and began his MLB career with the Royals in 1969.  

In 1971, he became the ace of the Royals’ pitching staff, going 17–11 with a 2.98 ERA and finishing fifth in the AL Cy Young Award vote. In 1972, he posted a 3.01 ERA and a 12–17 record. His performance declined in 1973 (12–14, 4.23 ERA), leading to a trade to the Boston Red Sox on October 24, 1973, for Marty Pattin.

He pitched for the California Angels and Baltimore Orioles in parts of two seasons. Acquired by the Orioles from the Angels on June 13, 1977, he filed for free agency after that season. He returned to Boston on November 21, 1977, and saved 13 games during his final three years with the Red Sox, finishing with a 10–6 record in 1979.  

He ended his major league career with the Seattle Mariners in 1981.

Throughout his 13-season career, Drago compiled a **108–117 record**, a **3.62 ERA**, and **58 saves** in **519 appearances** (189 as a starter).

Drago passed away on November 2, 2023, at the age of 78.
